title: Trading Risk Governance and Compliance
summary: How trading firms govern risk, set limits, control trades and protect clients. Education only, not advice.

modules.title: Three Lines of Defence and Board Oversight
modules.subject: Governance
modules.learned: Describe the three lines of defence, the role of board oversight and risk appetite, and why independence matters.

check.q: A trader sets her desk's limits and reviews her own breaches. Which principle is missing?
options: Independence, because the first line should not set and police its own limits
Speed, because limits must be acted on quickly
Profit, because limits reduce income
Disclosure, because limits must be published daily
check.explanation: A second line sets limits and challenges breaches, so the first line cannot mark its own homework.

modules.title: Limits, Thresholds and Escalation
modules.subject: Limits
modules.learned: Turn a risk appetite into limits with early-warning levels, explain value at risk and stress tests, and write an escalation path.

check.q: A desk's hard limit is 1,000,000 and its early-warning level is 750,000. Exposure is now 800,000. What is the correct response?
options: Nothing, because the hard limit has not been reached
Review the position in writing and explain it to the named owner
Raise the hard limit to 800,000
Double the position to reach a safer level
check.explanation: Crossing the early-warning level triggers a documented review while there is still room to act.

modules.title: Segregation of Duties and Trade Controls
modules.subject: Trade controls
modules.learned: Explain segregation of duties, the four-eyes principle, trade capture, reconciliation and access rights.

check.q: A trader amends a booked trade and then approves the amendment herself. What is the control failure?
options: None, because amendments are routine
Only the timing, because the amendment came after booking
The four-eyes check is missing, so the amendment is not independent
The broker's fees, which should have been higher
check.explanation: An amendment approved by its maker has not been checked by anyone else, so the four-eyes principle fails.

modules.title: Client Protection: Know Your Client and Conflicts
modules.subject: Client protection
modules.learned: Describe know-your-client, suitability and appropriateness, conflicts of interest, written disclosure and complaint handling.

check.q: A client with limited knowledge asks for a complex leveraged product, and the firm sells it without an assessment. What is the main failure?
options: None, because the client's insistence is enough
Only the price, because complex products are cheap
The client's choice, which the firm must never question
No recorded assessment of whether the product fits this client
check.explanation: The client's wish does not replace the assessment. The firm must check and record the fit before selling.

modules.title: Anti-Money Laundering: Risk, Due Diligence and Reporting
modules.subject: Anti-money laundering
modules.learned: Apply the risk-based approach, verify beneficial owners, apply enhanced due diligence, and escalate suspicion internally.

check.q: A corporate client's ownership chain ends in a company that will not name its owners. What is the right response?
options: Treat the relationship as higher risk, apply enhanced checks and escalate before accepting it
Accept the client, because the paperwork is complete
Accept it and stop asking about ownership after a year
Reject it and publish the reason
check.explanation: Unidentified beneficial owners call for enhanced due diligence and a senior decision under the risk-based approach.

modules.title: Monitoring, Incidents and the Governance Pack
modules.subject: Monitoring and reporting
modules.learned: Design a monitoring plan, run a breach log to root cause, explain record keeping, and prepare a governance pack with decisions.

check.q: A repeated booking error is corrected and logged as closed three times. What should the compliance officer do?
options: Accept each closure, because each error was corrected
Reopen the log, find the root cause in the process, and test the fix before closing
Dismiss the person who made the errors, without reviewing the process
Stop logging, because repeated errors are normal
check.explanation: Repeated errors point to a process gap. Only a fixed and tested process stops recurrence.

questions.q: In the three lines model, which line sets policies and limits and challenges the first line?
options: The second line, made up of risk and compliance functions
The first line, made up of the business and its traders
The third line, made up of internal audit
The board, acting alone without functions

questions.q: What does the third line of defence provide?
options: Daily trading limits set by the desk
Independent assurance to the board that the first and second lines work as described
Approval of every individual trade
Marketing support for new products

questions.q: What is a risk appetite?
options: The maximum profit a desk may earn in a year
A list of products the firm will not sell
The amount and type of risk the board is willing to accept to meet its objectives
The daily loss figure set by the trader

questions.q: Why must the second and third lines be independent?
options: So they can share the desk's bonus pool
So the first line can avoid reporting breaches
So the board never needs to read their reports
So they can challenge and review the first line without fear or conflict

questions.q: A risk officer's pay depends on the profit of the desk she checks. What is the issue?
options: A conflict of interest that must be recorded and managed
No issue, because risk officers are always paid by the desk
An issue only if the profit is negative
A tax issue, not a governance issue

questions.q: What is an early-warning threshold?
options: The level at which the trader is paid a bonus
A level below the hard limit that triggers review while there is room to act
The maximum loss the firm will ever accept
The price at which an option expires

questions.q: What does value at risk estimate?
options: The exact loss that will occur next week
The total capital of the firm
A loss not expected to be exceeded at a set confidence level over a set period
The average profit of all trades

questions.q: What does value at risk miss?
options: Any loss on a trade that has been closed
The premium paid on options
The daily settlement of futures
Tail losses beyond its chosen confidence level

questions.q: What is a stress test?
options: A calculation of loss under a large, specified market move, even if unlikely
A test of the trader's personal health
A check that the broker's systems are online
A review of each trade's entry price

questions.q: A desk passes its early-warning level late in the day. What is the right response?
options: Ignore it until the hard limit is reached
A written explanation to the named owner, with the plan, the same day
Raise the limit to fit the position
Add to the position to reach a safer figure

questions.q: What does segregation of duties prevent?
options: Traders from earning bonuses
Clients from opening accounts
One person controlling a transaction from start to finish, which can hide errors or unauthorised trades
Brokers from charging fees

questions.q: What makes a checker independent under the four-eyes principle?
options: The checker is the maker's closest colleague
The checker is the trader who originated the trade
The checker is chosen by the maker
The checker is not the maker and does not report to the maker

questions.q: What is trade capture?
options: Recording a trade in the firm's systems once, accurately and on time
Taking a photograph of the trading screen
Capturing the market's price movement
Selling the trade to a third party

questions.q: What is reconciliation?
options: Agreeing the trader's bonus with the head of desk
Comparing the internal record of trades with an external record, and investigating any breaks
Converting trades into another currency
Closing all positions at the end of the day

questions.q: Why are breaks aged?
options: So breaks can be carried forward without investigation
Because breaks are always resolved in a day
So an open break that lingers becomes visible to the second line
So the age of a break sets its value

questions.q: What does know-your-client verify?
options: The client's future profits, before the account is opened
The broker's licence, which the client must provide
The client's favourite instrument
The client's identity, purpose and relevant circumstances, before the account is accepted

questions.q: What is the difference between suitability and appropriateness?
options: Suitability applies where the firm advises, and appropriateness applies where the client decides without advice
Suitability applies to companies, and appropriateness applies to individuals
They are two names for the same test
Appropriateness applies only to futures

questions.q: When does a conflict of interest exist?
options: When two clients ask for the same product on the same day
When the firm's interest, or a staff member's, could compete with the client's interest
When a client disagrees with the firm's price
When a trader takes a day off

questions.q: What is a disclosure in client protection?
options: A press release about the firm's annual profit
A verbal confirmation after the first trade
A written statement of costs, risks or conflicts, given before the client decides
A list of the firm's staff

questions.q: Why is a cluster of complaints about one product significant?
options: It shows the product is performing well
It proves the clients are unreasonable
It has no meaning unless there are over a hundred complaints
It can reveal a control failure, such as a product sold without an assessment

questions.q: What is the risk-based approach to anti-money laundering?
options: Matching controls to the money laundering risk of each client, product and channel, and documenting the assessment
Applying the same checks to every client regardless of risk
Refusing all clients who make large deposits
Leaving controls to each individual staff member

questions.q: What is a beneficial owner?
options: The person who signs the account opening form
The natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client, or on whose behalf a transaction is carried out
The broker who executes the first trade
The company's external auditor

questions.q: What is tipping off?
options: Giving a client a copy of the account statement
Explaining the firm's fees to a new client
Telling a client or another person that a report has been made or is being considered
Sending a client a welcome email

questions.q: Which situation calls for enhanced due diligence?
options: A client who opens a standard savings account with a small deposit
A client who has traded with the firm for a decade without incident
A client who asks for a printed statement each month
A client with complex ownership that will not name its beneficial owners

questions.q: A staff member suspects a client's transactions are laundering money. What should happen first?
options: The suspicion is reported internally to the named person, and the decision is recorded
The staff member tells the client, to ask for an explanation
The staff member closes the account personally
The staff member waits a year to see if the pattern repeats

questions.q: What turns a monitoring plan into evidence?
options: Writing the plan and filing it with the board
Running each test on schedule against the records, and logging each result and failure
Testing only after a regulator visits
Relying on each trader's memory of their trades

questions.q: What should happen to a failure found in a monitoring test?
options: It is noted and fixed at the next annual review
It is discussed informally with the trader
It is logged the same day, with an owner, and closed only with evidence of the fix
It is ignored if the result was profitable

questions.q: What is a root cause?
options: The name of the person who made the error
The first symptom the trader notices
The date on which the error was discovered
The underlying process failure that produced a breach, as distinct from its trigger

questions.q: What should a governance pack contain?
options: Exposures, breaches, complaints and test results, each with a decision or action and an owner
Every email sent by the desk during the quarter
Only the firm's profit for the period
The full text of every policy, without a summary

questions.q: Why must records be retrievable?
options: Because records must be printed each day
Because monitoring, review and regulators depend on finding them quickly
Because records can be deleted once they are a year old
Because clients own all internal records
